title: How does the CAM driver certificate and its 35 hour periodic training work in Portugal?
description: Portugal's CAM driver certificate: initial qualification, 35 hours of periodic training every five years, code 95, and fines under Decree-Law 126/2009.
shortAnswer: Professional drivers of trucks and buses in Portugal need a Certificado de Aptidão para Motorista (CAM), the Portuguese form of the EU Driver Certificate of Professional Competence. Under Decree-Law 126/2009, as amended and republished by Decree-Law 102-C/2020, the CAM is valid for five years and is renewed through 35 hours of periodic training, after which the Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (IMT) records code 95 on the driving license.
keyTakeaways: Drivers of C1, C1E, C, CE, D1, D1E, D, and DE vehicles on public roads need the qualification, unless an Article 3 exemption applies.
Initial qualification is 280 hours (common route) or 140 hours (accelerated route), followed by an exam.
Periodic training is 35 hours every five years, taken before the CAM expires, with up to 12 hours by distance learning and up to 5 hours on high quality simulators.
Resident drivers prove the qualification with code 95 on the driving license, valid for five years; non-resident drivers working in Portugal receive a driver qualification card (CQM).
Driving without the qualification is fined EUR 500 to 1,500, reduced to EUR 50 to 150 if the document is shown within five days.
regulator: Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (IMT), with enforcement by the GNR and PSP
appliesTo: Professional drivers of goods vehicles in categories C1, C1E, C, and CE
Professional drivers of passenger vehicles in categories D1, D1E, D, and DE
Nationals of EU Member States, and third country nationals employed by an EU established company
Transport operators and other employers of professional drivers
Training entities certified to deliver CAM courses

sections.heading: What is the CAM and which law requires it?

blocks.text: The Certificado de Aptidão para Motorista (CAM) proves that a professional driver has completed initial qualification or periodic training. The rules are in Decree-Law 126/2009 of May 27, 2009, which transposed Directive 2003/59/EC. [Decree-Law 102-C/2020](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2020/12/23802/0022100257.pdf) of December 9, 2020 transposed the amending Directive (EU) 2018/645, made the second amendment to Decree-Law 126/2009, and republished it in full. Under its Article 9 it entered into force 30 days after publication.

Article 5(1) of the republished decree-law states that the CAM proves initial qualification or periodic training; Article 5(2) makes its issue depend on passing an exam after initial training or successfully completing periodic training; and Article 5(3) makes the qualification valid for five years from the exam or the end of periodic training. The Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (IMT) issues the CAM under Article 5(5).

The EU's European Commission database lists Decree-Law 102-C/2020, and [Decree-Law 121/2021](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2021/12/24800/0001900020.pdf) on driving alternatively fuelled vehicles with a category B license, as Portugal's transposition of Directive 2018/645. As at November 2026, those are the instruments this page relies on.

sections.heading: Who needs a CAM, and who is exempt?

blocks.text: Article 2 applies the regime to EU nationals, and third country nationals employed or engaged by a company established in a Member State, who drive on public roads vehicles requiring a C1, C1E, C, or CE license (goods) or a D1, D1E, D, or DE license (passengers).

Article 3(1) exempts drivers of vehicles in listed situations, including vehicles limited to 45 km/h; vehicles of the armed forces, civil protection, fire services, police, and urgent ambulance transport when used for those services; road tests and new or converted vehicles not yet in service; emergency and rescue use, including non-commercial humanitarian transport; driving lessons and exams; non-commercial carriage of passengers or goods; and carriage of the driver's own work materials where driving is not the main activity. Article 3(3) and (4) add exemptions for certain rural and agricultural, horticultural, forestry, livestock, and fishing transport within limits.
Exemptions turn on the purpose of the trip, not just the vehicle, so employers should record why a driver is treated as exempt rather than assume it.

Initial qualification is mandatory and has two routes under Article 6: common initial qualification and accelerated initial qualification. Annex II sets the common route at 280 hours, and Annex III sets the accelerated route at 140 hours, each followed by an exam organized by the IMT or entities it designates.

sections.heading: What are the rules for the 35 hours of periodic training?

blocks.text: Periodic training (formação contínua) is 35 hours every five years, taken before the CAM expires. Article 9(1) states that it is mandatory and must be attended every five years, before the end of the CAM's validity, to update knowledge with particular emphasis on road safety, safety and health at work, and reducing the environmental impact of driving.

Annex IV, point 2, of the republished decree-law states that periodic training "é obrigatória de cinco em cinco anos e tem a duração de 35 horas lecionadas por períodos de sete horas por dia": it is compulsory every five years and lasts 35 hours, taught in periods of seven hours a day, which may be split over two consecutive days. The other rules in Annex IV are:

items: Point 1: training updates and revises subjects from the initial qualification syllabus, and the subjects on road safety and on rational fuel consumption are mandatory.
Point 3: up to five hours may be taken on high quality simulators, and up to 12 hours using distance learning tools.
Point 4: periodic training for renewing the CAM is valid for five years from the date it is completed successfully.

blocks.text: Article 9(2) allows a lapsed CAM to be renewed through periodic training within a maximum of five years from the end of validity of code 95 on the license or of the CQM.

sections.heading: How does a driver prove the qualification at the roadside?

blocks.text: Article 4(1) provides that the qualification is proved by code 95 recorded on the driving license, for drivers resident in Portugal, or by a driver qualification card (carta de qualificação de motorista, CQM) for non-resident drivers who work in Portugal and complete periodic training there. Article 4(4) makes the code 95 entry or the CQM valid for five years and dependent on holding a CAM. Article 4(7) requires third country drivers of goods vehicles to prove qualification through the EU driver attestation showing code 95.

Article 26(1) gives the IMT oversight of the regime and gives the Guarda Nacional Republicana (GNR) and the Polícia de Segurança Pública (PSP) roadside enforcement of the Article 4(1) qualification duty.

sections.heading: What should a transport operator track for each driver?

blocks.text: A transport operator should track CAM and code 95 expiry for each driver and plan periodic training well ahead, since a lapsed qualification stops the driver working. The table summarizes the obligations, the timing, and the evidence to hold.

blocks.text: Set the refresh trigger well before expiry; [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) and [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) explain the method. CAM periodic training also covers safety and health at work, which overlaps with the employer's general duties in [Portugal's OHS training requirements](/regulations/portugal-ohs-training-requirements).

sections.heading: What are the penalties for driving without a valid CAM?

blocks.text: Article 27(1)(a) fines driving in breach of the Article 4(1) qualification duty at EUR 500 to 1,500, reduced to EUR 50 to 150 if the driver shows the document to the authority named by the officer within five days. Article 27(1)(b) applies the same fine to driving a D or DE vehicle in breach of the 50 km regular service limit for younger accelerated route drivers. Under Article 27(2)(a), a training entity operating without the required certification is fined EUR 10,000 to 30,000. Negligence is punishable with the limits halved, and under Article 29 the driver may have to pay or deposit the fine at the roadside, failing which the vehicle may be seized.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the CAM syllabus as defined topics, with road safety and fuel use flagged as mandatory in every cycle, and links each driver's periodic training to the CAM and code 95 expiry dates. Distance learning and simulator hours are recorded against their caps, so the 35 hour cycle can be shown to meet Annex IV.

faqs.q: Is the CAM the same as the EU Driver CPC?
faqs.a: Yes. The CAM is Portugal's certificate of professional competence under the EU rules on initial qualification and periodic training of professional drivers, originally Directive 2003/59/EC and amended by Directive (EU) 2018/645. Code 95 on the license is the EU wide mark that the driver holds the qualification.

faqs.q: Can CAM periodic training be done online in Portugal?
faqs.a: Partly. Annex IV of the republished Decree-Law 126/2009 allows up to 12 of the 35 hours using distance learning tools and up to five hours on high quality simulators. The rest must be classroom or practical training delivered by a certified entity.

faqs.q: What if a driver's CAM has already expired?
faqs.a: Under Article 9(2) the CAM can still be renewed through periodic training within a maximum of five years from the end of validity of code 95 or the CQM. The driver may not drive professionally in the meantime, since the Article 4(1) qualification duty would be breached.

faqs.q: Do bus and truck drivers need separate periodic training?
faqs.a: At initial level, Article 11(1) states that a driver who already holds a goods CAM and wants a passenger CAM, or the reverse, only has to attend and pass the subjects specific to the new qualification. Drivers holding both should confirm with their certified training entity how a single periodic training cycle is recorded for each.
